findings.title: Validate public artifacts with their live renderer browser contract
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the public build mode and approved-input identity available to browser/accessibility/performance consumers, and select a public-artifact test configuration that derives routes and assertions from that input. Retain the existing fallback suite for fallback artifacts; do not reuse its Fixture variants, Select variant or fixed-origin assertions against public live output. Add a release-gate integration check that serves a compiled public artifact and exercises the selected browser contract.

findings.title: Give formal staging proof a matching execution context
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the borrowed proof command with a formal-publication staging proof entry point/configuration. Supply run-bound buyer and any required failure-fixture inputs with corresponding staging preparation/cleanup, or scope the suite to publication-relevant journeys that do not require those legacy fixtures. Add an explicit protected formal-publication authority path to the latency wrapper, retaining exact source/target/run checks and the existing rehearsal restrictions rather than setting a false rehearsal flag. Verify both staging-source activation and production-source proof-only restoration using the actual job environment.

findings.title: Preserve existing public carts when the storefront changes
findings.suggested_fix: Use a distinct public-storefront catalog header for the compiled marker, and consume it for public product lookup and current-release new-line qualification. Reserve X-Preview-Catalog-Release and assertUsableCart's strict release equality for actual private preview sessions; allow existing public CartToken reads, updates and checkout to keep their already-qualified historical catalog. Add a Worker-to-API regression covering an A cart after B activation and after rollback, and retain the private preview cross-release rejection test.

findings.title: Close ordinary failures before storefront mutation begins
findings.suggested_fix: Give the delivery step an ID and add a same-run failure callback inside each protected publication deployment job when an earlier step fails and the delivery step was skipped. Use the existing fail command only for this proven pre-mutation case; preserve the runner's restoration/unresolved handling once delivery started. Cover an expired production backup and a failed pre-delivery baseline/artifact step, asserting that the producer leaves building and permits a new request after verified safe failure.

testing_gaps: tools/storefront-publication.ts:588-884 contains the executable capture/deliver/recover composition, including report/input binding, a fresh same-run owner check, proof-only restoration and the special uncertain-receipt recovery branch. tools/storefront-publication.test.ts exercises the helpers individually, while tools/deploy-workflow.test.ts:1225-1304 checks workflow strings/order. A scratch CLI harness with fake transport/commands would add distinct protection: assert no deployment on mismatched report/input or changed owner, no producer callback during proof-only delivery, and no restore after an accepted receipt or uncertain outcome. Invoke that entry point from publication-staging while leaving the existing CI-GH rehearsal-only entry point and its guards intact; do not fabricate rehearsal flags to bypass its intentionally different authority. Add a non-network authority test using the actual publication job environment.

findings.title: Pre-delivery job failure permanently strands the pending publication

Cover publication-staging for staging-source requests and publication-production pre-delivery failures; keep post-mutation/unknown outcomes on the existing retained-baseline unresolved recovery path. Add workflow/state integration scenarios for browser-install failure, backup rejection and baseline-capture failure, verifying that a safely failed request permits a new attempt and an unverifiable storefront remains unresolved.
